body.statement: For every array satisfying the growth, fraction, boundedness, and nondegeneracy conditions, \[G_n\sigma_n^2=R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n}+o(1).\] More precisely, \(G_nC_{\tau\tau,n}+\rho E_{\tau,1,n}\to0\) and \(C_{11,n}/p_n+C_{00,n}/(1-p_n)\to0\); all Johnson degrees \(k\ge2\) vanish at the \(G_n\)-scale uniformly over the bounded schedules.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(d_n=h_{1,n}-h_{0,n}\) and
\[
 e_{k,n}=\|\Pi_{n,k}d_n\|_n^2,
 \qquad k=1,\ldots,M.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:bounded-potential-outcomes} and the definition of a group mean give \(|h_{z,n}(A)|\le B\) for every \(z\) and \(A\).  Hence
\[
 V_{z,n}=\operatorname{Var}_n\{h_{z,n}(A)\}\le B^2
\]
and, by the orthogonal decomposition in Definition~\ref{def:johnson-decomposition},
\[
 \sum_{k=1}^M e_{k,n}
 =\operatorname{Var}_n\{d_n(A)\}
 \le \mathbb E_n[d_n(A)^2]
 \le 4B^2.                                                    \tag{1}
\]
Because \(N_n=MG_n\le n\), fixed \(M\), and \(G_n\to\infty\) by Assumption~\ref{ass:group-count-growth}, one has \(n\to\infty\).  We may therefore restrict attention to \(n\ge4M\).

For \(1\le k\le M\), Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-kneser-identity} and the falling-factorial formula give
\[
 |\lambda_{n,k}|
 =\frac{(M)_k}{(n-M)_k}
 =\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{M-j}{n-M-j}.
\]
For \(n\ge4M\), every denominator in this product is at least \(n/2\), while every numerator is at most \(M\).  Consequently
\[
 |\lambda_{n,k}|\le \left(\frac{2M}{n}\right)^k.             \tag{2}
\]
In particular, using \(G_n=N_n/M\le n/M\), (1), and (2),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \left|G_n\sum_{k=2}^M\lambda_{n,k}e_{k,n}\right|
 &\le G_n\left(\frac{2M}{n}\right)^2
       \sum_{k=2}^M e_{k,n}\\
 &\le \frac{n}{M}\frac{4M^2}{n^2}\,4B^2
 =\frac{16MB^2}{n}.                                         \tag{3}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Since \(\lambda_{n,1}=-M/(n-M)\), the covariance identity in Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-kneser-identity} and (3) yield the uniform deterministic expansion
\[
 G_nC_{\tau\tau,n}
 =-\frac{MG_n}{n-M}e_{1,n}+O(n^{-1})
 =-\frac{N_n}{n-M}E_{\tau,1,n}+O(n^{-1}).                   \tag{4}
\]
Here and below the constants in the \(O(\cdot)\) terms may depend on the fixed \(M\), \(B\), and the limiting treatment fraction, but not on the bounded potential-outcome schedule.

The same spectral argument controls the two arm covariances.  Indeed,
\[
 C_{zz,n}
 =\sum_{k=1}^M\lambda_{n,k}
   \|\Pi_{n,k}h_{z,n}\|_n^2,
 \qquad
 \sum_{k=1}^M\|\Pi_{n,k}h_{z,n}\|_n^2=V_{z,n}\le B^2.
\]
Equation (2) therefore implies
\[
 |C_{zz,n}|\le \frac{2MB^2}{n}.                             \tag{5}
\]
By Assumption~\ref{ass:stable-treatment-fraction}, there are \(\delta>0\) and \(n_0\) such that \(p_n\ge\delta\) and \(1-p_n\ge\delta\) for \(n\ge n_0\).  Thus (5) gives
\[
 \left|\frac{C_{11,n}}{p_n}
       +\frac{C_{00,n}}{1-p_n}\right|
 \le \frac{4MB^2}{\delta n}=O(n^{-1}).                     \tag{6}
\]

Multiplying the exact identity in Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-pame-variance} by \(G_n\), and using \(G_{1n}=p_nG_n\) and \(G_{0n}=(1-p_n)G_n\), gives
\[
 G_n\sigma_n^2
 =R_n+G_nC_{\tau\tau,n}
   -\frac{C_{11,n}}{p_n}-\frac{C_{00,n}}{1-p_n}.
\]
Substitution of (4) and (6) proves the sharper, schedule-uniform formula
\[
 G_n\sigma_n^2
 =R_n-\frac{N_n}{n-M}E_{\tau,1,n}+O(n^{-1}).                \tag{7}
\]
No nondegeneracy condition is needed for (4)--(7); Assumption~\ref{ass:scaled-variance-nondegeneracy} is needed only by the downstream standardized limit and coverage results.

It remains to recover the displayed claim with its limiting coefficient.  Assumption~\ref{ass:sampling-fraction} and fixed \(M\) imply
\[
 \frac{N_n}{n-M}
 =\frac{N_n/n}{1-M/n}\longrightarrow\rho.                 \tag{8}
\]
Since \(E_{\tau,1,n}=e_{1,n}\le4B^2\) by (1), equations (4) and (8) show
\[
 G_nC_{\tau\tau,n}+\rho E_{\tau,1,n}
 =O(n^{-1})+\left(\rho-\frac{N_n}{n-M}\right)E_{\tau,1,n}
 \longrightarrow0.                                        \tag{9}
\]
Equation (6) proves the other asserted vanishing term, and (7)--(8) prove
\[
 G_n\sigma_n^2=R_n-\rho E_{\tau,1,n}+o(1).
\]
The bound (3) separately certifies that every Johnson degree \(k\ge2\) is uniformly negligible at the \(G_n\)-scale.

For completeness, the same primitive bounds also give the rate needed to locate the CR2 phase elbow.  Fix \(z\in\{0,1\}\), put \(m=G_{zn}\), and let \(f\) be either \(h_{z,n}\) or \(h_{z,n}^2\).  Marginally, the \(m\) groups observed in arm \(z\) form an exchangeable ordered disjoint sample, so
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\!\left\{\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m f(A_j)\right\}
 =\frac{\operatorname{Var}_n(f)}m
  +\frac{m-1}{m}\langle f^{\circ},\mathsf K_nf^{\circ}\rangle_n. \tag{10}
\]
The spectral bound (2), applied to \(f\), shows that the absolute value of the second term is at most \(2M\operatorname{Var}_n(f)/n\).  Boundedness of \(h_{z,n}\), stable treatment fractions, and \(G_n\le n/M\) therefore make (10) \(O(G_n^{-1})\), uniformly for both choices of \(f\).  Chebyshev's inequality gives the arm empirical first- and second-moment errors as \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2})\).  Since \(m/(m-1)=1+O(G_n^{-1})\), the definition of \(s_{z,n}^2\) then yields
\[
 s_{z,n}^2-V_{z,n}=O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2}).               \tag{11}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 G_n\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-R_n
 =O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2}),
\]
and combining this relation with (7) gives
\[
 G_n\bigl(\widehat V_{\mathrm{CR2},n}-\sigma_n^2\bigr)
 =\frac{N_n}{n-M}E_{\tau,1,n}
  +O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2}+n^{-1}).                       \tag{12}
\]
Thus no condition on \(N_n^2/n\) enters this variance comparison. In the mesoscopic regime \(N_n=o(n)\), if \(E_{\tau,1,n}\to e>0\), the deterministic correction in (12) has order \(N_n/n\), while the proved stochastic remainder is bounded by order \(G_n^{-1/2}\asymp N_n^{-1/2}\). These two displayed rates meet at \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\), giving a benchmark crossover. Because (11) is only an upper bound, no matching lower noise order or exact below/above elbow claim is asserted.
body.justification: The degree-one Johnson projection is the unique first-order memory of finite-pool competition, and the exact coefficient \(N_n/(n-M)\) yields a schedule-uniform \(O(n^{-1})\) remainder rather than only a limiting \(\rho\)-formula.
body.gap: \cite{FuSamiiWang2026} covers this design only as the homogeneous \(K=1\) member of a broader fixed finite size menu and obtains inference through \(N_n^2/n\to0\) plus its Assumption 1.  The present predictable-variation regime is an assumption trade, while the Kneser calculation retains the dense dependence discarded by whole-tuple coupling.
body.consumer: The exact coefficient determines the correct standard-error comparison at positive density. The proved \(O_{\mathbb P}(G_n^{-1/2})\) fluctuation upper bound gives \(N_n\asymp n^{2/3}\) as a useful benchmark crossover when \(E_{\tau,1,n}\to e>0\), without asserting a matching noise-order lower bound.
